title: The Balance of Good and Evil
text: “Nano, it’s true Gaelion doesn’t know if that bottle in the room was real or not. But could you really tell it would self-destruct, nano?”
“Hmph… if you knew the circumstances, it would be obvious he was attempting an assassination, would it not? Recall the look in his eyes at that moment.”
“True enough… that king’s potential to return as a hero in various ways is obvious to anyone, nano, so it’s no surprise he’d feel more threatened by that than by Naofumi, nano.”

“In which case, I simply slipped into the tea party he arranged, and had the king or queen somehow overlooked things, I would have poisoned him myself with the very act I’d seen through… the result would have been the same either way. Well, there was also a good chance the king would intervene beforehand and things would turn out just as they did, so it was within expectations.”

“True… if Rafumi-chan, the culprit, hadn’t been there, Atla-chan would definitely have been in danger. If that poison had been left in his hands as it was… the king, the queen, Melty-chan, and Fohl-kun would all have been in danger.”
“He just shouldn’t have been given it in the first place, nano. In the end, the king only noticed and ate it anyway, nano.”

“He seemed to have had a faint suspicion, so he apparently gave the order himself to try and reduce his sentence. Because of that, the king’s mentally stuck on the idea that he killed himself with his own hands… I’m a little worried whether he’ll recover.”
Even in this loop, Father was showing remarkably gentle consideration despite having every reason to hold a grudge, I say. Father truly did sympathize with Trash, indeed.
“I suppose it’s best to say I saw through it, hm? Well, Motoyasu-kun looks incredibly frustrated.”
“Frustrated, indeed!”
The Crimson Swine should have been made to suffer far more, I say!
“Is this really something a Hammer Hero should be doing, I wonder… or rather, is it even something Ren’s body double should be doing?”
“As long as it isn’t discovered, it’s fine. Precisely because I have no intention of stirring up trouble, I confronted you now rather than back then, didn’t I?”
Grrrgh… indeed! What a wicked spirit, I say! Rafumiiiii!
“Nano, Gaelion really thinks you have too much of a wicked side to you.”
“Heh… let me teach you something. Not all of a spirit’s nature is good. It is precisely because evil coexists within that balance is maintained.”
“Yes yes, nano. Just be careful you don’t turn into an evil spirit, nano.”
“You needn’t say it. If I’m to be honest, I rather wanted to try it. Still, putting foreign objects into food makes even me want to retch. Bleeeeeeergh.”
With a perfectly composed face, Rafumi vomited up chocolate.
“Whoa, vomiting chocolate with a completely blank expression… Rafumi-chan, are you overdoing it?”
“Cough.”
“You… what is it, being damaged while looking totally unfazed?”
“Cough! This too… is part of my revenge… cough.”
Was she genuinely taking damage, I wonder?
“Even against her own pride, to go through with something she clearly hates so much…”
“Do not forget what kind of spirit I was, one who raged with fury over such things. I will not forgive anyone who treats chocolate carelessly. Do not put strange things into food.”
“Nano, Gaelion’s decided not to ask why you’re still vomiting in real time, nano.”
“So it’s really the method of poisoning—putting foreign substances into food to make people eat it—that you hate most, Rafumi-chan.”
“Correct. You knew that already, didn’t you?”
That would be about the household of the thief that Father took under his wing, I gather, indeed.
“Is it because you’re so lenient about Ren running off on his escapades, since you take food seriously that you’re willing to be generous?”
“Naturally. I intend to lend my cooperation wherever delicious food is being made.”
“I suppose that’s just Rafumi-chan’s own rule, huh… well, Motoyasu-kun, let’s give up on this one for now.”
“Damn it all, I saaaaay!”

The Crimson Swine got away from me, I say! Having to endure until the next loop is truly maddening, indeed. Come to think of it, I’ve barely made that swine pay at all, I say! The loop after I poisoned it, it had already been disposed of, and just when I was fully prepared to make it suffer properly, this happens, I say.
“Well, as for the king, I’ll also show him some consideration in various ways.”
“Nano, Gaelion’s starting to feel uneasy about whether it’s really okay to leave that to you.”
“If I push him too far, the staff’s spirit gets noisy about it. I won’t play around that much. Besides, he still has a spiritual pillar supporting him, so he’ll manage well enough as things stand.”
A spiritual pillar, I wonder? So Trash still has someone propping him up before being reduced to a hollow shell, I say?
“Nano, Gaelion thinks it’d be better to have them meet later. What happened this time was quite dangerous, nano.”
At Rival’s words, Rafumi wore an unpleasant smile, I say.
“Don’t say that. It was something Tiger Girl wished for in the very first world—an earlier appearance. Wouldn’t it be fine to grant that wish?”
“True, Gaelion won’t deny Tiger Girl’s wish, but… nano.”
They seemed to be discussing something only Rafumi and Rival understood, I say.

“Spear Hero, you might want to give this some thought as well. What, it’s simple—just don’t show it to that princess. No, actually… if the opportunity arises, showing it to the king even earlier might prove rather amusing, wouldn’t it?”
“Rafumi-chan really does like sticking her foot into danger, doesn’t she…”
I felt as though Tiger Girl had made some sort of request to me, but… ah, it was about the lavish lifestyle of royalty, indeed. I made that happen again this loop too, I say!
“Well, what we must be careful about isn’t so much while she’s in Melromarc, but rather it’d be far more dangerous to drag her around while she’s on the Siltvelt side.”
“That’s far too dangerous a matter, involving internal politics, nano.”
“I’m having a bit of trouble following what you’re all talking about…”
Father seemed unable to join in on the conversation between Rafumi and the others, I say.
“It’s the same in this loop too, isn’t it? Bringing Atla and Fohl around Siltvelt as subordinates of the Shield Hero is dangerous, is it not?”
“Well, the people connected to Siltvelt and Wolf keep saying as much. That it’s extremely dangerous from an internal political standpoint.”
Tiger Girl and the others’ race, the Hakuko, apparently had issues with their standing in Siltvelt, meaning it was particularly dangerous to bring them along as Father’s subordinates there, indeed.

“Since I brought them along for the sake of exchange with the king, it’s true I’d like them to stay on the Melromarc side. Or perhaps it’d be best to have them treated as subordinates of Lars-chan or someone like that. Lars-chan knew about it too and was keeping an eye on things.”
That would be because Panda and Tiger Girl’s group had all sorts of connections, I say.

“Well… let’s leave the matter of that princess’s poisoning at that for now. Is there anything else to discuss? At the next location, Cal Mira Island, Rafumi-chan, make sure you bring Ren along properly, okay?”
“Understood. The personnel to bring to Cal Mira Island, was it.”
“Nano, the numbers are a bit much so we need to think it through. Spear Hero, are you going to do the Filolial Fever thing there again, nano?”
“I did it in search of Filo-tan, but since Filo-tan is already here in this loop, I’m troubled over what to do, indeed.”
“Given how many Filolials there already are, I’d really rather you didn’t add even more…”
We all put on a show together to liven things up, I say.

“Or rather, what should we do after visiting Cal Mira Island? The queen asked me to keep the restoration of Éclair-san’s territory to a reasonable degree and instead challenge the waves in other countries.”

Ah, I received that very same sort of request from the queen in the very first world as well, indeed. No doubt I’ll be asked the same before departure this time too, I say. In this loop, it’s Ren—Rafumi—who’s become the hero the queen wants kept in Melromarc, indeed.

“Nano, you could simply travel between countries until the waves are over. Also, Gaelion doesn’t think anyone would complain if you helped with restoration efforts, so there shouldn’t be a problem. As for Gaelion’s own thoughts—Naofumi, where do you plan to set up your base from now on, nano?”

That’s certainly a good question, indeed. Restoring Big Sister’s group’s village was something he did fairly often, and afterward using the village as a base to go handle problems in various regions seemed to be the general pattern, I say.

“That’s exactly the thing, isn’t it… in terms of responsibility, Raphtalia-chan’s group’s village is the easiest option, but Wolf and the people of Siltvelt want me to come to Siltvelt, and Shion seems to want me to come here for the sake of restoration too…”
Father seemed to be troubled, going “hmmm,” indeed.
“Nano, Gaelion’s going to head over to Shieldfreeden’s side, tagging along while looking after Bow Hero.”

“I’m thinking of having Theo and Rishia-san accompany Itsuki too. Apparently Itsuki’s planning to help with the restoration of the Roomo-species people in this country as well. Can Shieldfreeden accept Roomo-species people?”
“Nano, Gaelion wouldn’t really recommend it. The docile temperament of the Roomo-species here isn’t suited for settling down there, nano.”
I too had memories of Shieldfreeden, which Takt and that pig had governed, indeed. Even without the matter of reparations, the place was already a mess, I say.
